description: We are a motivated team participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge, focusing on wildfire detection and satellite data. Our goal is to build an innovative solution using NASA's MODIS and VIIRS data to monitor and analyze wildfires. We welcome team members skilled in coding, AI, UI/UX design, data analysis, or presentation. Join us to share ideas, collaborate, and build something impactful!
summary:
Firesight answers one question: is this fire season normal? NASA has 26 years of satellite fire detections from two sensors: MODIS since 2000 and VIIRS since 2012. VIIRS sees far more fires, so in the raw data every year since 2012 looks worse than it was. In Greece the count jumps 2.4x in 2012 because the sensor changed, not the fire.

Firesight harmonizes both into one consistent record, from November 2000 to yesterday, for Portugal, Greece, Lebanon and Cyprus. We put both sensors on the same 1 km grid, measured how many more fires VIIRS sees per month and country where both flew, and used that factor to convert the older MODIS years. On held-out years, Greece's yearly error fell from 61% to 6%.

We built a website and an Android app. Pick a place and a month and get one clear sentence: how it compares with the usual. They add a fire danger forecast, alerts, ground reports with photos, an open API, and English and Arabic.

This matters because civil protection teams, farmers and residents can only plan if they know whether a season is truly unusual. A sensor change should not look like a fire crisis.
details: WHAT IT DOES Firesight turns NASA FIRMS fire detections into one consistent 26-year record and answers "is this fire season normal?" for a country, or for any box you draw inside it. It comes as a website and an Android app. HOW IT WORKS 1. One unit: every detection is snapped to a 0.01° grid (about 1 km) and counted once per day per sensor (an "active-fire cell-day"). This removes most of the extra counts from VIIRS's smaller 375 m pixels. 2. Calibration: over every month since 2012 where both sensors flew, we compute VIIRS ÷ MODIS for each calendar month and each country. The factors range from x1.47 in Portugal to x5.5 in Lebanon, so one global factor would be wrong everywhere. 3. Converting the past: years before 2012 are MODIS × that month's factor. Terra-only years (before July 2002) get their own factor. 4. Continuity: VIIRS outage days are filled from MODIS. After Suomi-NPP stopped in November 2026, NOAA-20 VIIRS carries the record. 5. Validation: we left out one year at a time and predicted it from MODIS alone. Yearly error went from 34% to 6% in Portugal, 61% to 6% in Greece, 84% to 17% in Lebanon, and 71% to 26% in Cyprus. WEBSITE FEATURES One-sentence verdict for any month, the last 7 days against every other year, "Fire Rings" (fire history drawn like tree rings), a year × month burning calendar, a raw/harmonized switch that shows the 2012 jump, a season profile, a 16-day fire danger forecast (Canadian Fire Weather Index), live near-real-time hotspots, air quality, CSV/PNG exports, an open JSON API, a web console for organizations (fire stations, insurers, NGOs), and full English and Arabic (right-to-left). MOBILE APP (Android, Flutter) Download (APK): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Qsks4bCU_lHrqUPh1iOvusAAKHWTqSg0/view?usp=sharing- Today: the one-sentence answer for your location (GPS), Fire Rings, season chart, fire weather and burn advice.- Calendar: the year × month record, with the raw/harmonized switch that shows the 2012 jump.- Map: hotspots from the last 48 hours on NASA GIBS imagery, with your position and ground reports.- Alerts: above-normal activity, "critical period starts in N days", and hotspots near you. Watched places are checked in the background every 3 hours.- Field verification: a photo, GPS position and label (wildfire, farm burn, industrial, false alarm), linked to the satellite hotspot, to build ground truth.- Smoke location: each smoke report records the compass direction the phone points. Reports from two or more places are crossed to estimate where the fire is, and the app shows whether a satellite has seen it yet.- 7-day burn planner: picks the safest day this week for farm burning, leaving out days with strong wind, dry air or the critical period.- Works offline (cached data and map tiles). One tap to call or text your location to Civil Defence (125). Full Arabic, right to left. BENEFITS AND IMPACT Fire agencies, farmers, researchers, insurers and the public can compare a season with the true long-term normal instead of a record distorted by the change of sensor, and act on it from their phone. TOOLS TypeScript, React, Vite, MapLibre, Hono, SQLite, Node.js and Docker (website and API). Flutter/Dart, flutter_map, Firebase Cloud Messaging and WorkManager (mobile). Data refreshes every 6 hours from the FIRMS API. LIMITS WE SHOW OPENLY It counts detections, not hectares burned. Cloud and smoke hide fires. Small-fire countries (Lebanon, Cyprus) are less accurate. Near-real-time data is corrected later by NASA. This is an independent project, not a NASA product. USE OF AI Parts of the code and text were written with help from Claude (Anthropic)
